Progress note · simulation-validation arm

Dipole theory, and the same estimator run on a dark-matter box

Two weeks: a tested linear-theory prediction for ζ̂1 (with a sign error in Nusser 2017 found and corrected), what each cosmological parameter does to it, the estimator run unchanged on a constrained Gadget-4 particle box, and a recipe for deciding when a shell near r = 0 is a measurement.

Ofek Einav 23 August – 7 September 2026 521 tests passing

isrc/dvcorr/theory/ · tests/test_theory.py

The linear-theory calculation

Everything from a linear P(k) to a predicted multipole is now a tested library, built on one k-integral and validated twice before anything used it — against closed forms per Bessel order and per power of k, and against brute quadrature on the real CAMB spectrum (~10−6). The FFTLog tilt had to be derived from the spectrum’s own slopes rather than left at the library default, which at (ℓ, p) = (1, −1) is wrong by ~105 and silently sign-flipped.

Mℓp(y) = ∫0∞ dk kp P(k) jℓ(ky)the one integral
(ℓ,p) = (1,1) → A(y) · (2,0) → B(y)y · (1,−1) → Ψ⊥y/f²
Ψ′⊥ = −f²B,    Ψ′− = −f²(A − 3B)
Górski (1988), checked through Ψ− = y Ψ′⊥ across three independent FFTLog orders

Nusser (2017) eq. (17) as printed has the wrong sign on the Ψ′− coefficient. With it corrected, the B (i.e. j2) terms cancel exactly — for every b and every f — and only j1 survives. That cancellation, evaluated two independent ways and agreeing to machine precision, is what pins the correction; the printed sign leaves a residual that makes the redshift/real ratio scale-dependent.

b/f + 3/5 − 3(b/3f + 1/5) = 0exactly, ∀ b, f
the coefficient of B in the redshift-space dipole
⟨ξsuδg⟩1(y) = (aH f / 3)(b + 3f/5) A(y)
real space is the b + 3f/5 → b limit — one shape, two amplitudes

Bottom line

The linear prediction is a tested function rather than a formula copied from a paper — and a sign error in that paper was found on the way, by a cancellation that only closes when the sign is right.

iiintuition/linear_theory_parameter_scans.ipynb

What each cosmological parameter does

Real space factorizes exactly: b, f and σ8 enter only through one scalar and none of them touches the shape. σ8 is quadratic because both legs derive from the same δ; b is linear because the velocity leg is unbiased. Asserted, not eyeballed — 33 curves over f ∈ [0.3, 0.8], σ8 ∈ [0.65, 0.95], b ∈ [0.6, 2.1] collapse onto one shape to <10−10. Ωm is the exception: it moves the shape too, through keq ∝ Ωmh.

ζ1(r) = (aH / 6π²)(b f σ8²) Ŝ(r),   Ŝ(r) = ∫dk k P̂(k) j1(kr)
σ8[P̂] = 1 — the shape carries no parameter at all
ζ1s / ζ1 = 1 + 3f/5b = 1 + 3β/5flat in r to 4×10−16
linear RSD is a pure amplitude rescaling; a measured ratio that is not flat is a bug
ζ3s ∝ (2/5) f²σ8²,   ζ3 ≡ 0
the octupole is bias-free and identically zero in real space — a zero-parameter check

Bottom line

ζ1 alone measures b f σ8² and nothing else, so fitting b to it is circular. Redshift space adds a second combination, b f + (3/5)f², and the ratio of the two is a clean β free of σ8 — the argument for building the λ-dial run.

iiinotebooks/DM_simulation.ipynb · dvcorr.pipeline.dm_snapshot

The dark-matter simulation

The existing pipelines, unchanged, on the constrained Gadget-4 box: 256³ particles in 300 h−1 Mpc at z = 0, built from 2MRS, so its centre is meant to be us. Only the loader is new — no estimator forked, no frozen convention edited. The tracer field is the matter field (b = 1), which is the reason to run it: every MDPL2 measurement is of biased tracers and this one is not.

ẑobs = sgn(u) n̂V, w = |u|   vs.    ẑvel = v̂, w = |v|
the only difference between the two frames: the axis and the scalar
ζ1vel / ζ1obs = 3   (⟨μ²⟩ = 1/3),    ζ0vel / ζ0obs = 2measured 2.80 / 2.00
the observer frame projects twice for the dipole, once for the monopole
σ(vr) / 100 = 3.37 h−1Mpc
the rms radial displacement — the fingers-of-God scale on a particle field

The projection ratio straddles its geometric baseline (2.32 at r ≈ 3 → 3.69 at r ≈ 36) rather than climbing away from it, so it is not a constant that can be divided out. Redshift space is the strong result: fingers-of-God do not merely damp the dipole, they reverse its sign inside r ≈ 8 h−1 Mpc, with Kaiser winning out past r ≈ 22. As a geometry check, ⟨|u|⟩/⟨|v|⟩ = 0.503 against the isotropic 0.500.

Bottom line

Same code, different simulation, unbiased tracers — and the redshift-space effect MDPL2 shows only weakly appears here at full strength, with the sign flip where the displacement scale says it should be.

ivdvcorr.pipeline.robustness · notebooks/10_small_scale_robustness.ipynb

Virialization near r → 0

This began as a near-miss: the innermost bin read 301.9 km/s on one centre set and 80.4 on a 58% subset of the same centres. So I wrote the general recipe for deciding whether a shell is a measurement — precision ladder, bootstrap interval over centres, trim ladder, independent redraws, and a mechanism split on a variable measured at a different scale from the shell under test. Four of the five cost no extra estimator pass.

j1(0) = 0  ⇒   ζ̂1(0) = 0∀ P(k), b, f, σ8
a dipole needs a direction; coincident points define none. The curves are now drawn into it.
σ(ζ̂1) ∝ Nc−1/2  ⇒   10× centres → ±87 km/s
clean over a 50× range, so the cure is priced rather than guessed

On the particle field, resolving down to the softening: both original numbers were noise (expected 1σ wander ~1150 and ~1510 km/s), but a real feature appears that a lumped bin cannot show — ζ̂1 peaks at r ≈ 0.46 h−1 Mpc and falls inside it, in all four independent draws and at every trim depth. The split names the cause: contribution rises with environment, then goes negative for the most crowded centres, which sit deep inside massive halos where neighbours orbit rather than infall. On MDPL2 halos the same five tests give the opposite answer — the ordering is strictly monotone at every measured shell, so if halos do it, it lives inside r ≈ 0.14 h−1 Mpc, which 108,743 centres cannot see into.

Bottom line

Virial cancellation is real on the matter field and not seen on halos above r ≈ 0.14 h−1 Mpc. Both are scale statements with a priced cure, not open questions.

Next

  • The λ-dial run — the same catalog with the displacement on and off; acceptance is a ratio constant in r, equal to 1 + 0.6β.
  • 10× the centres near r → 0, the one thing between us and a measured depth for the turnover.
  • An independent b, since ζ1 constrains only the product — the DM box’s matter autocorrelation is now the calibration target.

All of it is in the repository; numbers are printed in the notebooks rather than read off figures, and the suite (521 tests, including the infall sign gates) passes. Happy to walk through any of it.
